summary: Make credential-home resolution (CODEX_HOME and, symmetrically, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) a single canonical seam shared by every consumer - session spawn, Settings Test, Usage, Terminal-tab Login, oauth_dir/env CRUD validation, and Settings display - so an ambient/leftover env value can never leak into a session, terminal, or probe, and the two credential-bearing agent kinds behave identically. Storage: provider_instances.oauth_dir keeps storing the user's literal (unchanged column, no migration, no auto-repoint of existing rows); reads canonicalize it (expandTilde/canonicalizeOauthPath/effectiveCredentialHome) and upsert validates the resolved home (non-empty, absolute, unique among enabled rows of the same agent kind, and the canonical default reserved for the default row) before writing - identically for Codex (~/.codex) and Claude (~/.claude), and for either source (an oauth_dir column or a legacy env-mode row's own CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR overlay value). An unchanged, already-enabled legacy row sitting on the reserved default is exempt from re-validation on a cosmetic edit or disable, so a stale profile stays repairable in Settings without forcing a relocation first; moving a row onto the reserved directory, or creating a new one there, still fails. That advertised repair action is also made safe: because env values never cross IPC, a cosmetic save arrives with an empty env map, so an update carries the row's stored CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR forward when the incoming map omits the key (envToStore), validates the home it will actually store rather than the one the caller sent, and refuses the save outright when the stored overlay cannot be decrypted - a rename can no longer silently move a legacy profile onto the shared default account. Rollout: unconditional, with no feature flag anywhere in the repo; shipped in v0.8.54 (see CHANGELOG.md), and this manifest's updateRelease surface now records that release rather than deferring it. API: IPC wire is additive-only - ProviderInstanceWire/ProviderInstance gained effectiveOauthDir plus effectiveOauthDirSource ('oauth_dir' | 'env' | 'default' | 'unresolved', now part of the shared @shared/types contract instead of main-only), and TerminalCreateOptions gained loginInstance (identity-only; main resolves env for both Claude and Codex, the renderer never builds CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR itself). State: resolveProviderInstance throws (never silently substitutes the default) when an explicitly requested instance id is missing, disabled, or the wrong agent kind; the machine-default instance id is now scoped per agent (chat.defaultProviderInstanceId.<agentType>) so a Codex pick made through the pre-scoping global key can never prefill a Claude/OpenCode session, while still honoring that legacy key when it still names an instance of the requesting kind. UI: Settings Providers renders credential home per effectiveOauthDirSource for both Codex and Claude rows - an oauth_dir home as a plain isolated path, a legacy env-overlay home labeled as such (still isolated, no warning), the shared canonical default with an explicit isolation warning, and an unresolved row as 'cannot verify' rather than a guessed directory - never an env value or account identity. CREATE_OAUTH_DIR stays home-confined (lexical .. collapse plus a real-symlink-escape check via realpathSync) and creates at 0700; the Terminal-tab Login flow sends only identity across IPC and rejects (with created-state cleanup: routing-table unbind, no half-built xterm instance or registry entry) rather than opening an unscoped shell on a bad id. Lifecycle: packaged/Finder-launched Codex discovery also searches the user's login-shell PATH (parity with the OpenCode adapter) via a non-blocking peekShellEnv/warmShellEnv probe that never blocks the event loop (a blocking loadShellEnv form remains only for the one-shot machine connect/provision paths); remote Codex auth also checks a keyring-only login via `codex login status` (async, cached, single-flighted per config dir, bounded by a hard timeout) rather than only auth.json presence. Tests: unit coverage added across all of the above, including a fail-first regression proving Claude gets the same reserved-canonical-home and unchanged-legacy-row-stays-editable treatment as Codex, a Settings-display contract keyed off effectiveOauthDirSource rather than the raw oauthDir column, a real-filesystem (non-mocked) symlink-escape proof for CREATE_OAUTH_DIR, and a fetchInstanceUsage-level proof that simultaneously-configured Codex instances resolve distinct CODEX_HOMEs under an ambient leftover CODEX_HOME.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android app (apps/android) is a thin remote client for both credential-bearing kinds: it never touches a local CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or oauth_dir path, and never spawns a provider CLI itself. It sends only an instanceId over the same shared backend wire contract this feature hardened (ProviderInstance/ProviderInstanceWire, START_SESSION/SUBMIT_USER_TURN, the provider-instance-switch contract) and inherits resolveProviderInstance's strict-explicit-id behavior, resolveInstanceEnv's canonical-home resolution for Claude and Codex alike, and the per-agent-scoped machine-default key with no native code change. No native-Android-specific credential-isolation gap exists to fix, so none was introduced or touched in this pass.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema migration and no auto-repointing of any existing row, for either agent kind. The provider_instances.oauth_dir column keeps storing exactly the literal string the user typed (rowToWire's comment: 'wire keeps the literal so the user sees what they typed'); upsertProviderInstance's validateCredentialHome only rejects a NEW or MOVED save whose resolved home is empty, non-absolute, a duplicate among enabled rows of the same agent kind, or the reserved canonical default (~/.codex or, now identically, ~/.claude) claimed by a non-default row - it never rewrites a stored value, never migrates a legacy env-mode row to oauth_dir, and explicitly exempts an unchanged already-enabled row (even one already sitting on the reserved default or already duplicating another row) so existing rows keep saving cosmetic edits with no forced repoint. The one write-path invariant on existing rows is preservative, not migratory: an update whose env map OMITS the structural home var (CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) carries the stored value forward instead of dropping it (envToStore), because env VALUES never cross IPC so no caller can re-send one, and a cosmetic Settings save therefore arrives as `env: {}` - overwriting the blob with that silently repointed a legacy env-mode profile at the shared canonical default from its next spawn on. Naming the key still repoints the home and naming it blank still clears it, every other key still follows the documented `{}`-clears/`null`-keeps contract, and a save whose stored overlay cannot be decrypted at all is refused rather than allowed to replace an unverifiable home. Canonicalization (expandTilde/canonicalizeOauthPath/effectiveCredentialHome) is applied only at read/resolve time, is idempotent, and needs no backfill: a pre-existing row with a relative or tilde-prefixed oauth_dir, or a legacy row whose home lives only in its env overlay, resolves correctly the first time this code runs.

Reviewed and deliberately deferred as nonblocking, with no code change in this pass: (a) the LIST IPC path resolves 'unresolved' effective homes eagerly, so a boot-time Settings/StatusBar refresh can decrypt a legacy overlay and touch the OS keychain once per launch on an unsigned build - the memo only covers subsequent calls, and making it lazy needs a separate resolve channel plus renderer wiring; (b) deleteProviderInstance does not repoint conversations that referenced the deleted id, so with the new strict resolveProviderInstance such a thread errors on its next send instead of falling back (recoverable in-product: the rail stays visible and the picker repoints it); (c) implicit (no-id) resolution can still return a DISABLED `<kind>-default` row while resolveVisibleLoginInstanceId filters to enabled, unreachable today because Settings exposes no disable control; (d) resolvedHomeMemo in ipc/providerInstances.ts is unbounded (one entry per row version); (e) the mobile 'context-unavailable' rotation code is overloaded across 'no live session' and 'credentials unavailable for a safe rollback', matching desktop's pre-existing behavior, so a DB-only repoint can disagree with a still-running session until it ends; (f) a login PTY receives the instance's full decrypted overlay rather than only the home var, which is the intended behavior for a shell that must reproduce the profile.
